subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Which Telegram formatting modes should OpenClaw support publicly, and should account-level settings override a channel-wide default?
rationale: This determines the escaping/trust boundary and a long-lived plugin configuration contract; source and discussion show that rich delivery alone does not answer those product choices.

options.title: Safe default plus plain-text opt-out
options.body: Keep the current safe rich/HTML-compatible behavior as the default and add only a clearly documented plain-text opt-out, deferring raw HTML and MarkdownV2.

options.title: Support multiple explicit modes
options.body: Add plain, safe HTML-compatible, and MarkdownV2 modes with per-account precedence, each with documented escaping and delivery semantics.

options.title: Do not add a mode selector
options.body: Keep one formatter and address concrete rendering defects individually through the existing Telegram delivery path.

recommendation.title: Safe default plus plain-text opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the current safe rich/HTML-compatible behavior as the default and add only a clearly documented plain-text opt-out, deferring raw HTML and MarkdownV2.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue review records this exact public-contract decision as unresolved product direction.
